title: Nine Marks on the Ruler
subtitle: 计量与单位 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 计量与单位（科学与技术·计量与单位）
meta: 主题语境：计量与单位（科学与技术·计量与单位）　|　核心词汇：centimetre　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 centimetre 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 my mother was sent to measure ① centimetre she could not find, and she said the measuring was the whole of the lesson. The ② centimetre, meaning the unit and not the length, was nine marks long and was measured by whoever came last; centimetre, she said, is the only thing on a ruler that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ centimetre on that ruler had the same mark, and the ④ centimetre at the end, meaning the one the surveyor kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever measured properly. Centimetre, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ centimetre was the whole of the plan, meaning the length it stood for and not the unit. The ⑥ centimetre, meaning the length and not any of that, is the only thing in a plan that everybody agrees on and nobody questions; centimetre, he said, is either something you measure or the only word that means both a unit and a length. She said the length is the part they remember.

By 1967 the ⑦ centimetre had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the mark. The ⑧ centimetre of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine marks and eleven years of measuring; centimetre, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ centimetre I remember is the one at the end, which was measured in 1972 and is still described as the shortest in the county. A ⑩ centimetre, my grandmother said in 1977, is the only thing that improves by being measured; every centimetre, she said, is a length that has agreed to look like a unit. She said the length was the honest half.

answers.why: measure a centimetre 意为“量出一厘米”，1952 年母亲被派去量她找不到的那一厘米。
centimetre 意为“厘米”，指那个刻度单位本身而不是那段长度，共九格，由最后来的人量。
centimetre 指尺子上每一格，每一格都是同样的记号。
centimetre 指末尾那一格（测量员保留的那一格），是唯一有人认真量过的。
centimetre 意为“长度”，抽象指它代表的那段长度，父亲说 centimetre 就是那份图纸的全部。
centimetre 为抽象用法，指那段长度本身，是一份图纸里人人都认可、却没人质疑的东西。
centimetre 意为“厘米”，到 1967 年这一厘米成了报告里的一个数字。
centimetre 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九格记号和十一年的测量。
centimetre 意为“厘米”，我记得的是末尾那一格，1972 年量过，至今仍被说成全县最短的。
centimetre 为抽象总称，祖母说一厘米是唯一会因为被认真测量而变好的东西。
